incident-bot: Paging: HIGH - routing fallback triggered in us-west-2, affected customers on Dedicated. More details incoming.
Maya Patel: grabbing context. @Alex can you confirm impact window + mitigation notes for customer followup?
Alex Chen: oncall handoff here — issue started 2026-03-10T14:08:43Z. Autoscaler backlog + a regression in route-compile led to >50% elevated 503s for short window. Mitigation: scaled dedicated pool, reverted compile throttle patch at 14:22Z, traffic stabilized by 14:30Z.
Samir Gupta: thanks — do we have an initial customer-facing timeline and what customers saw (errors vs latency)?
Alex Chen: customers saw intermittent 503s for requests routed through fallback; latency for successful requests up ~200ms. Total affected requests ~0.7% of traffic for the window.
Maya Patel: draft customer message below. Please add edits. We want short, empathetic, and specific on impact and credits.
Maya Patel: "Hi — we experienced a service disruption in us-west-2 that affected Dedicated model endpoints between 14:08Z and 14:30Z on 2026-03-10. During the window some requests returned 503 errors and you may have seen higher latency on a subset of requests. Root cause: an interaction between the routing compile backlog and autoscaler limits. Mitigation: we scaled capacity and reverted the compile throttle, which restored normal traffic by 14:30Z. We are taking the following actions to prevent recurrence: 1) revert/patch compile path to avoid backlog, 2) adjust autoscaler thresholds for routing backpressure, 3) add monitoring alert for compile-queue growth. We will follow up with an RCA and timeline within 72 hours. We apologize for the disruption and will credit affected usage. — Redwood Inference Ops"
Samir Gupta: The draft is good. Suggest adding exact SLA credit steps and a public status page blurb. Also remove internal phrase "compile" for the initial customer-facing message, replace with "request routing backlog" to be less technical.
Maya Patel: updated draft with wording change + status blurb. "Status page (for customers): Incident: Routing backlog caused request failures in us-west-2 (14:08Z–14:30Z). Impact: Intermittent 503 errors and elevated latency for some Dedicated endpoints. Mitigation: scaled capacity and rolled back routing throttle. Next steps: full RCA and customer credit evaluation."
Alex Chen: +1. For the RCA we'll include timeline, root cause analysis, mitigations, and tests. I'll attach log snippets to the RCA doc.
Maya Patel: internal exec template (short): "Summary: Brief statement of impact and customer scope. Root cause: short sentence. Actions taken: list. Customer impact: windows, error rate, mitigation. Next steps: fixes + monitoring + credits. Owner: ops + eng leads. Target: RCA in 72h."
Samir Gupta: can we be explicit about credit mechanics? e.g., "Customers with >0.5% error rate due to this incident will receive a pro-rata credit for affected requests; CS will coordinate case-by-case."
Maya Patel: added credit language. @ops-bot please schedule the RCA doc review with eng and cs for 2026-03-11 16:00Z.
ops-bot: RCA review scheduled: 2026-03-11T16:00:00Z. Invite sent to Maya, Alex, Samir, eng-leads.
Alex Chen: quick note for timeline accuracy: mitigation started at 14:22Z (scale + rollback), traffic within normal bounds by 14:30Z; we'll attach TTL of autoscaler events.
Maya Patel: request to legal/PR — is there anything else we should avoid in the initial message? @Samir please triage.
Samir Gupta: legal OK with wording; PR suggests we avoid promising exact credit amounts until engineering quantifies affected usage. fine to say "credit evaluated and applied as appropriate".
Maya Patel: final check — are we good to post status page and send customer emails using the draft?
Alex Chen: yes from eng side.
Samir Gupta: good from CS. I'll coordinate sending to customers who had affected endpoints and flag enterprise accounts for personalized outreach.
Maya Patel: posting status page update now and preparing customer email batch. I'll attach the final RCA link here after review.
incident-bot: Status page update posted: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-03-10-routing-backlog
Maya Patel: thanks team. Follow-up actions assigned: Alex -> compile patch + autoscaler threshold PR; Samir -> customer outreach + credit queue; Maya -> RCA doc and exec summary. Standby for the RCA link. :thumbsup:
Alex Chen: will add post-deploy tests to ensure routing queue doesn't reach threshold.
Samir Gupta: scheduling 1:1 with affected customers tomorrow to walk through timeline if they request it.
Maya Patel: closing thread for now, will reopen when RCA doc is ready."
